newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore oil products mixed as LSWR drop.
newsitem.headline: Singapore oil products mixed as LSWR drop.

text.p: Singapore oil products were mixed on Thursday with low sulphur waxy residue falling on reduced demand from Japan, while gas oil rose on crude strength, traders said.

Physical gas oil traded at $32.20 a barrel for 150,000 barrels lifting Jan 10-14 fob and later traded lower at $32.40 for Jan 19-23. Discussion on Tuesday was in the $32.25-range. Gas oil swaps also rallied with January traded at $32.08 and $32.10 up from Tuesday's $31.75/$31.85 quotes. Traders said prices were also supported by India's second tender for February after buying 720,000 tonnes in its first February tender.
Regional was also seen from Nepal and Sri Lanka which has issued tenders to buy diesel and jet-kerosene fuel for February and mid-January respectively.

LSWR dominated the fuel oil market talk with of 3.5 million barrels expected in Indonesia's January allocation, traders said. They said BP has been allocated 1.1 million barrels. They said LSWR prices, currently assessed at $23.00-$23.20 a barrel were likely to ease further in January as they expected Pertamina to allocate another 500,000 barrels in January at a later date. They said the total of 4.0 million barrels would suffice to meet the lower demand from Japan and the west.
They said Japan is expected to import around 1.2 million barrels in January. South Korea is likely to import 500,000 barrels on spot and 1 million on a term basis.

Naphtha firmed notionally on stronger crude values but there was physical trading as many players were away for the Christmas holidays. January swaps was bid at $24.50, up from Tuesday's $23.80/24.10 per barrel.
Malaysia's Petco awarded a nine-month term tender to sell 50,000-tonne a month of naphtha from its Malacca refinery but did not award cargoes from Kertih.
